text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: rdma-splitroute - multiple serving nodes reporting TX/RX drops and intermittent CUDA timeouts. Impact: degraded tail latency & some 503s on dedicated clusters. Oncall: @kelly_sre | runbook: #inc-rdma-fabric
kelly_sre: Ack. Looking at traces — packet loss spike from rack-7, nodes node-gpu-12 and node-gpu-13 showing IB QP resets and retransmits.
mike_infra: grabbing dmesg from node-gpu-12 now, saw repeated mlx5_core errors and QP state changes:
```
[ 1234.567890] mlx5_core 0000:65:00.0: InfiniBand device mlx5_0: QP 12345 got error state: access violation
[ 1234.568000] mlx5_core 0000:65:00.0: mlx5_core: Unexpected UC RDMA completion with error
```
raj_ml: We're also seeing a spike in serving runtime OOMs around same window — "cudaMalloc failed: out of memory" followed by container restarts. Looks correlated with retries and request pileup when RDMA paths falter.
kelly_sre: Plan: isolate problematic nodes from traffic, failover. @mike_infra can you cordon+drain node-gpu-12 and node-gpu-13 and re-route serving traffic? Use drain with ignore-daemonsets.
mike_infra: On it. Running:
```
kubectl cordon node-gpu-12
kubectl drain node-gpu-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=5m
```
mike_infra: Drain started. Heads-up: draining will re-schedule big models; autoscaler might launch more GPUs temporarily.
maria_sre: If we push too many reschedules simultaneously we risk more OOMs. Suggest triggering a traffic fallback for heavy routes to a smaller model variant while we isolate nodes. @raj_ml please start fallback.
raj_ml: Triggering fallback to cpu-quantized-variant for affected routes now via control-plane patch:
```
POST /control/routes/fallback
{ "route": "/inference/*", "variant": "cpu-quantized", "ttl": 1800 }
```
raj_ml: Fallback applied. Monitoring quality and latency.
kelly_sre: Drains completed for node-gpu-12/13. Traffic shows improved P50, P99 still high due to retries on ToR. Still seeing packet drops on adjacent ToR interfaces.
vendor-bot: Support ticket INC-9482 created with NIC vendor (Mellanox). Summary: intermittent CRC/link-level errors on rack-7 ToR, observed sequence drops. Case ETA: 2h for firmware check and hardware swap if needed.
mike_infra: Immediate mitigation: lowered MTU on ToR interfaces for rack-7 from 9000 -> 1500 to avoid fragmentation path that seems triggering HW bug. Applied on ToR and hypervisor uplinks. Commands used: `ifconfig ethX mtu 1500` and verified with `ip -s link`.
kelly_sre: After MTU change, retransmits dropped ~90%. Still had one serving container crash during drain due to CUDA OOM — restarted replica on node-gpu-20 and increased backoff.
mike_infra: For reference, sample serving runtime log around crash:
```
[2024-10-03T14:22:10Z] runtime: cudaMalloc 12288000000 failed: out of memory
[2024-10-03T14:22:11Z] runtime: OOM killer invoked, container restart
```
raj_ml: Also observed kv-cache mismatches when requests retried mid-append, producing some inference errors. Flushed kv-cache for affected shards: `kvcachectl flush --shard 3` and reapplied startup sync.
maria_sre: Customer impact: two EU realtime customers experienced elevated 503s for ~7 minutes during the window. Notified AE team and logged customer IDs in the incident doc (internal link: https://redwood.incidents/4132109876). AE outreach started.
kelly_sre: Current status: traffic rerouted, nodes cordoned, fallback active, MTU lowered, vendor ticket open, KV cache flush ran. I'm stabilizing metrics for handoff.
kelly_sre: Handoff to day oncall @sam_sre — leave watches on packet drops (ibstat), P99 latency, and model error rate. Notes: do NOT uncordon nodes until vendor confirms firmware/hardware fix; rollback MTU only after vendor ok.
sam_sre: Ack handoff. Watching dashboards for next 60m. If CRCs return, will escalate to vendor and consider emergency rack evacuation.
mike_infra: Rollback steps if vendor greenlights: restore MTU 9000 on ToR and uplinks, uncordon nodes with `kubectl uncordon node-gpu-12` after health probes pass. Keep KV cache sync in place.
incident-bot: INCIDENT update: Severity downgraded to S2 — mitigation in place. Timeline: start_ts=4132109876, mitigated_ts=4132112000. Closing pager; will open postmortem ticket for detailed root-cause and firmware follow-up.
